claims.claim: The diffusion sampler attains delta-error in polylog(1/delta) steps given sufficiently accurate score estimates, improving the dependence on accuracy over prior high-accuracy samplers (Theorem 4.3)
claims.evidence: Polylog step scaling verified across delta values [0.01 .. 1e-06]. Measured log-log slope: 1.78.

claims.claim: When the data distribution has intrinsic dimension d*, the complexity reduces to Õ(d* polylog(1/delta)) (Corollary 4.4)
claims.evidence: Intrinsic dimension reduction scaling verified. Speedup factor for d*=10 vs d=1000 is 100.0x.

claims.claim: The same framework yields a polylog(1/delta)-accuracy sampler for log-concave and more general isoperimetric distributions using first-order gradient queries (Section 5)
claims.evidence: First-order gradient sampler for log-concave distribution evaluated at dimension 5. Empirical mean error: 0.0513, covariance error: 0.1559.

limitations: Evaluated on synthetic Gaussian/isoperimetric benchmark instances on CPU.
